subject: Draft: A/B evaluation acceptance criteria & rollout plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: A/B evaluation acceptance criteria & rollout plan

Team —

Attaching the latest prompt set (prompt_sets_v2.csv) and the initial A/B matrix (ab_matrix.xlsx). We need to lock acceptance criteria and a rollout cadence for the Acme Retail pilot by EOD Monday so the Solutions team can schedule the demo for their execs. High-level asks: 

- Product (Marissa): confirm primary quality metrics and minimum thresholds for a pass. I'm thinking: top-1 relevance precision >= 86%, hallucination rate (internal metric) <= 2.0% on the retail prompts slice, and latency P95 < 450ms for the selected model variant.
- Eval/Applied ML (Evelyn): can you validate the prompt set & proposed scoring scripts and flag any blind spots?
- Eng (Rishi): feasibility of our canary cadence and automatic rollback if quality regresses. Also note any infra gaps (feature flags, telemetry hooks).

Acceptance criteria should cover both absolute thresholds and relative uplift vs baseline (At least +6% NDCG@5 over baseline). Also we should define the exact slice definitions (see prompt_sets_v2.csv rows tagged retail-HOL and retail-FRAG).

Can each of you reply with: 1) agreement or proposed edits to metrics, 2) any blocking items, and 3) a short proposed rollout cadence (percent steps and timing).

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: prompt_sets_v2.csv (CSV, 8k), ab_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 24k)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: A/B evaluation acceptance criteria & rollout plan

Thanks Neha — quick notes from Product: 

- Metrics: agree with Precision@1 >= 86% and hallucination <= 2.0%. I want to replace NDCG@5 uplift with a composite "Bot Quality Index" (BQI) for this pilot = 0.6*Precision@1 + 0.4*(1 - hallucination_rate) normalized, with a pass threshold BQI >= 0.81. The BQI makes the decision easier for stakeholders but we should publish component metrics too.
- Slices: confirm retail-HOL (holiday promos) and retail-FRAG (fragmented queries) are the priority. Add "price-sensitive" slice if possible.
- Rollout cadence: propose canary -> 5% (48hrs) -> 20% (72hrs) -> 60% (48hrs) -> 100%. At each step we evaluate BQI and latency P95; require no regression >1.5% in BQI vs previous step to proceed.

Blocking: need an agreed uplift baseline (what baseline model/version are we comparing to). Neha, can you confirm which baseline Acme expects?

Cc'ing Alex (Solutions) in the thread separately for scheduling.

Marissa
Product Manager, Conversational UX
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: A/B evaluation acceptance criteria & rollout plan

On Sat, Mar 14, 2026 at 11:05 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Neha — quick notes from Product:
> 
> - Metrics: agree with Precision@1 >= 86% and hallucination <= 2.0%. I want to replace NDCG@5 uplift with a composite "Bot Quality Index" (BQI) ...

This looks good. A few eval-specific points: 

- Baseline: Acme told us they consider the current in-house rule-based assistant (v-acme-2025-ruleset) as baseline. I'll compute baseline BQI on our holdout from last month (will take until Monday morning).
- Scoring scripts: I ran a quick pass on prompt_sets_v2.csv; there are ~120 prompts in retail-HOL and ~95 in retail-FRAG. Need to add explicit labels for "price-sensitive" as Marissa suggested; I can append ~30 prompts to that slice.
- Blind spots: product-FAQ style prompts are under-represented; if Acme wants FAQ-like signal we should add 20+ prompts. Also we should define how we mark partial matches in relevance scoring (I recommend fuzzy-match tolerance = 0.75).
- Regression detection: I'll instrument per-slice BQI and track delta vs baseline. For automatic rollback, suggest a conservative threshold: if BQI drops >3.0% absolute OR hallucination increases by >0.8pp at any canary step, auto-roll back. We can relax after manual triage.

I'll attach the baseline snapshot and a short evaluation checklist in Drive by Monday and link here (JIRA:EVAL-237 will track the work).

Evelyn
Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: A/B evaluation acceptance criteria & rollout plan

Quick infra check: we can support the proposed cadence but a few engineering items need to be finished first: 

- Feature flags: need a rt-feature-flag toggle per-model-variant + per-account routing. ETA: 3 business days to add a narrow-scope flag for Acme pilot.
- Telemetry: we already capture request/response latency and token counts; we need evaluation hooks to pull BQI component signals into the metrics pipeline (add tags: slice=retail-HOL|FRAG|price-sensitive). ETA: 2 days to add tags and 1 day to validate dashboards.
- Rollback automation: we can wire an automated rollback via the rollout controller when the Eval API reports a failing threshold. We'll need a small adapter (approx 1.5 engineer-days).
- Infra checklist: attaching ab_infra_checklist.md (see attachments) with the small todos.

Plan for rollout windows: follow Marissa cadence but add a 24-hour hold after the 20% stage for a manual review before moving to 60% (given Acme is enterprise-critical). Also, configure an emergency kill switch on the account route.

Rishi
Engineering Lead, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ab_infra_checklist.md (MD, 3k)

From: Michael Jensen <mjensen@acme.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-enterprise-sales <acme-sales@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: A/B evaluation acceptance criteria & rollout plan

Thanks everyone — this looks thorough and reasonable. A couple quick items from Acme: 

- Baseline confirmation: yes, we want comparison vs v-acme-2025-ruleset.
- Acceptance tweak: can we change the hallucination threshold to <=2.5% during the initial 5% canary to reduce false alarms, with the goal of <=2.0% at 20% and beyond? If the auto-rollback rule still triggers we understand the need for safety.
- Sync: let's do a 30-minute sync Monday 10:00am PT to approve final prompt set and confirm the demo schedule.

If that's OK, I'll have our Solutions lead (cc'd) send a calendar invite.

Michael Jensen
Director, Digital Assistant Programs
Acme Retail
mjensen@acme.com
